name: Strict Source-System Spectral Criteria
statement: Let $R_i$ be finite families of nonnegative rows. A positive system $h_i<mh$ for every $m\in R_i$ is feasible exactly when the minimum spectral radius over all nonempty closed row choices is greater than one. A negative system $v_i>mv$ is feasible exactly when the maximum spectral radius over all full row choices is less than one. Empty row families impose no inequality; the empty positive minimum is $\infty$ and an empty negative system has threshold zero.
proof: A feasible vector and a nonnegative left Perron vector give necessity. If a strict system is infeasible, the strict linear alternative produces nonnegative row weights. Rowwise averaging and a resolvent perturbation select a closed positive choice of radius at most one, while rowwise maximization against a right Perron vector selects a full negative choice of radius at least one.
